notes: Six own pages read for classing plus three cited pages read in the first pass for the C01 cause (bakerhill.com/banks, an own page that now names UN/FY, and two aloan.ai comparison pages), all HTTP 200 and not thin. The first pass classed C01 stale on the vendor's November 6, 2025 release, which announces UN/FY and the retirement of the NextGen name in 2026 without a day, and recorded aloan.ai/compare/meridianlink-alternatives (a competitor comparison page, typed other, cited by seven of the fifteen answers carrying C01) as its cause. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026) re-classed C01 to unverifiable and cleared its proof, stale_change and cause fields: the release dates the announcement, not the retirement, the partner page read on 8 Oct 2026 still names Baker Hill NextGen in the present tense, and the UN/FY page says it is built on NextGen, so the pages read do not show the name was retired by the 22 to 23 Sep 2026 capture date. C03 stays true because the release itself describes UN/FY as the evolution of the LOS for NextGen clients. No browser reads exist for this vendor, and the gaps file and the answers' tables and sub-headings add no in-scope statement.
